classification: Unmodified pinned upstream tee with original WASI cwd and closed-stdout descriptor adapter
changes: No upstream parser, stream loop, output writer or error-mode changes.
Original WASI entry initializes cwd from PWD through the existing family helper.

When stdout is initially closed, the original WASI entry holds a real read-only cwd descriptor in fd1 so output-file opens cannot reuse stdout. The normal filesystem rejects writes to this descriptor. No synthetic write result, mode or ownership is installed.
Upstream WASI reads at most 32 KiB per iteration and writes that slice to each output before another read.
GNU tee is an independently verified test oracle only, never a runtime fallback.
unsupported: WASI does not implement upstream native signal-ignore installation for -i. Waffle supervisor cancellation remains authoritative.
Linux splice/tee zero-copy optimization is not built on WASI.
GNU SIGPIPE process-status parity is not claimed. Closed descriptors and actual broken pipes are tested separately.
The runtime has one virtual principal and supported owner-mode bits, not Unix ownership, groups, ACLs or device files.
Diagnostics, help and version are uutils text, not GNU text.
Closed stdout diagnostics can report a directory or rights error rather than native EBADF; bytes, status and output-file effects are compared.

On a stdout error with --output-error=exit, pinned upstream completes writes of the current read slice to later outputs before returning failure. GNU stops before those writes. The runtime test verifies both results explicitly.
